data.name: Hafzah
data.gender_notes: Hafzah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who memorizes the Quran. The name Hafzah carries the meaning “Preserver” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Hafzah usually hope their child will grow to embody preserver and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A woman deeply committed to her faith and the preservation of sacred texts
data.etymology: Hafzah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Preserver.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hafzah total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The title Hafzah carries a significant weight in Islamic culture, as it acknowledges a deep dedication and commitment to preserving the divine words of Allah (God). Hafzahs are revered for their remarkable memory and the ability to recite the entire Quran from memory, making them spiritual guardians of the Islamic faith.
data.spiritual_significance: Hafzah refers to an individual who has internalized the Quran and made it an integral part of their being. It symbolizes a deep level of devotion and connection to Allah, as well as a commitment to spreading the message of the Quran to others. This spiritual significance is a reminder of the importance of knowledge, memorization, recitation, and living the religion as a whole.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Preserver" symbolizes One who memorizes the Quran. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Hafzah serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of preserver.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that She was a prominent female reciter of the Quran in the Islamic Golden Age. The name Hafzah carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Islamic Golden Age was a period of cultural, economic, and scientific flourishing in the history of the Islamic world, primarily during the 8th to 14th centuries.

trends: used as a given name for girls
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Hafzah remains relevant in modern Muslim society, representing a bridge between traditional Islamic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Islamic names.

name_in_real_life.story: Zainab Hafzah, a teacher in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, shares that their name Hafzah meaning "Preserver" has been a source of inspiration throughout their life, motivating them to be a positive influence in their community.
